title: Observability: per-route metrics tags, structured logs, and streaming resilience for OpenAI-compatible API
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: improve end-to-end observability for the API surface (both OpenAI-compatible adapter and native Redwood endpoints) with three concrete goals: 1) ensure request/trace propagation and per-request metadata flows through streaming paths; 2) emit structured JSON logs with stable fields for downstream analysis and SLI calculation (including tool/function-calling events); 3) tag metrics per-route and per-compatibility-path to make latency/cost SLOs actionable. Scope: middleware and adapter layers, logger v2, metric tagging, small streaming protocol additions, tests and docs. Major points: - Request ID and trace propagation: unify headers (X-Request-Id, X-Redwood-Trace, Traceparent) at the edge, persist request_id on streaming sessions, and include request_id/trace_id in all emitted metric labels and structured logs; non-breaking fallback for older clients. - Streaming resilience signals: add periodic keepalive marker events and chunk-level health tags (stream_chunk.seq, stream_chunk.checksum, stream_chunk.type) so consumers and observability can detect mid-stream truncation and replays. - Structured logging: introduce json logger with stable schema: timestamp, level, request_id, trace_id, route, model, user_id (if available), op (e.g., inference.start, inference.chunk, tool.invoke), tool_invocation_id, duration_ms, token_count, error_code. Tool/function calling: emit explicit tool.invoke/return events with tool-specific metadata and route labels. - Per-route metric tagging: middleware adds route and compatibility labels (openai_compat=true/false; adapter_variant=classic/v2) to histogram and counter buckets so dashboards can split traffic easily. - OpenAI compatibility adapter changes: map openai's x-request-id and openai-client-metadata into Redwood trace fields, preserve streaming chunk framing but add minimal compat-preserving markers for observability; maintain same response framing for existing clients. - Rollout and feature flagging: feature-flagged via ff_obs_streaming; rollout ramp 10/30/60/100 over 48h with a kill-switch. Tests: unit + integration streaming tests added; added synthetic workload for streaming truncation detection. Backwards compatibility: header mapping is additive; clients that don't send trace headers work as before. Migration: analytics teams should pivot dashboards to use route and adapter tags. Related: ENG-9143 (per-route SLOs), ENG-9210 (streaming resiliency). Checklist: - [x] middleware to attach request/trace IDs - [x] json logger implementation - [x] per-route metric tags - [x] streaming chunk metadata and keepalive events - [x] openai adapter header mapping - [x] integration tests and docs - [x] feature flag and rollout plan
commits: feat(obs): add middleware for request and trace propagation across streaming sessions
feat(metrics): attach route and adapter tags to histograms and counters
feat(logging): implement json structured logger and replace plain logs in api handlers
feat(streaming): emit keepalive markers and chunk metadata in stream frame headers
chore(openai-adapter): map OpenAI headers to internal trace/request id fields
test(streaming): end-to-end truncation detection and replay tests
docs(obs): observability guide for API and adapter
review_threads: Priya: Overall looks good. Please add a short note on cardinality limits for route tags and ensure we aren't exploding metric label cardinality. Ava: Added a tag whitelist with rate-limited fallback and documented it in pkg/metrics/README.

Diego: Can we avoid changes in client-visible framing? The keepalive markers need to be no-op for existing parsers. Ava: keepalive is sent as a zero-length metadata frame with type=keepalive; adapter strips it for legacy frames. Added explicit tests.
Jordan: integration flakiness on Windows CI; suggest increasing the socket timeout in test harness. Ava: bumped timeout and added retry - tests stable now.
Priya: approve after addressing metric cardinality note. Diego: approved. Jordan: approved. Merge comment: squashed and merged by Ava after passing CI.
ci_checks: ci/integration: flaky first run, passed on rerun
release_notes: Add request/trace propagation across streaming sessions; request_id and trace_id included in structured logs and metrics
Emit streaming keepalive markers and chunk metadata for stream health monitoring
Introduce structured JSON logs with stable schema for API handlers and tool invocation events
Attach per-route and adapter tags to metrics for easier SLO dashboarding
OpenAI adapter maps OpenAI headers into Redwood tracing fields; backward compatible
notes_deploy: Feature-flagged rollout (ff_obs_streaming). Start 10% traffic for first 6h, 30% next 12h, 60% next 24h, full rollout after 48h if no regressions. Watch per-route latency histograms, streaming error-rate, and token throughput. Immediate rollback by disabling ff_obs_streaming.
migration_steps: Dashboard owners: replace raw /api/* histograms with route-tagged histograms
Client teams: no action required unless you rely on raw log text; JSON logger fields are additive
Observe the new streaming metric stream_chunk.truncation_count and alert if >0.1% for 1h
